headline: MGAT Alpha closed 12 trades this week for +$139.77 (83.33% win rate), the run's best week yet and the first time its all-time realized PnL has crossed into positive territory. All four position families closed positive for the first time in the run, and measured-beta coverage of new positions jumped to 92.86%, the highest of the run. But the book is still behind the plain alternative of having never traded: it sits at +0.64% since launch against a pinned hold-and-never-trade basket of its first seven coins, which is up 7.94% over the same period — a 7.3 percentage-point gap that widened slightly this week even as the trading result improved.

counterfactual.reason: The shadow comparison book is void for this run: it could never close a position, so none of its figures measure anything.

hold_benchmark.basis: $8,000 split equally across the seven coins the book bought in its first two cycles on 2026-08-25, held untouched, no fees

llm_adviser: LLM adviser: observer only — logs what it would do, cannot affect a trade (settled from source 2026-09-22).
sample_caveat: 12 closed trades this week, 58 all-time against the 200-trade target — 29% of the way to a sample size worth treating as meaningful, up from 23% last week. Win rate and PnL are past the point of being purely directional, but a single large loss could still swing the all-time read: all-time realized PnL is only +$2.67, and one closed trade earlier in the run lost more than $150 on its own, well over a full week's worth of this week's gain.
paper_caveat: Alpha is paper — simulated fills, no slippage, no thin-liquidity exits, no can't-sell-into-dust. A clean logic result here is never a claim that the execution floor works; that claim belongs to the Beta rung alone.
integrity: No entry in the repair ledger is tagged CLASS-A within this week's window, so the comparison with the prior week is clean on the trading logic. One repair-ledger entry does fall inside the window: a file revert on 2026-09-22 restored four source files to match the code that has been running unchanged since launch; the process was not restarted, so nothing the run executes changed, and the entry is not tagged CLASS-A. A separate CLASS-A entry (an earlier, unlogged change to the void shadow-comparison book) is dated by the change itself to before this window and carries no effect on the primary book judged here.

verdict.text: On every measure internal to the book this was an excellent week: ten wins on twelve closes for +$139.77, the run's first clearly positive week and the first time cumulative realized PnL has crossed above zero. All four families closed positive, all at a 75% win rate or better, inside a narrow band — the first week of the run with no family bleeding while another covers for it. Measured-beta coverage reached 92.86%, the highest of the run, meaning this week's sizing was overwhelmingly computed from real betas rather than guessed family weights, and only two minor faults fired all week with no criticals. What keeps the call at 'needs improvement' is the yardstick this run is now judged against: the book is +0.64% since launch, while simply holding its first seven coins untouched would be +7.94% — a 7.3 point gap that this week widened rather than closed, because the assets the book trades rose faster than the book itself did. The sample is also still small: 58 of 200 closes all-time, and all-time realized PnL of +$2.67 sits a single bad trade away from erasing itself, since one earlier trade alone lost more than this week's entire gain. A good week on the trading logic is not yet a case that the logic is adding value over doing nothing.
